core.title: Split L/XL features; decompose M features when necessary
core.given: A feature's footprint bracket is M (11-15), L (16-25) or XL (>=26).
core.when: The planner finalizes the feature's plan after sizing.
core.then: Split every L and XL feature; for an M feature, decompose it when decomposition is necessary.
prefer: For an M feature, actively assess whether decomposition is necessary. No authored criterion for necessity exists, so this is a judgment, but it is not a free pass: once necessity is established, decomposing is required.
avoid: Keeping an L or XL feature unsplit.
Keeping an M feature whole when its decomposition is necessary.
Retyping or dropping components to get under the split threshold instead of splitting.
core.why: Oversized footprints signal features too large to plan and deliver as one unit.
evidence: Features in L or XL are split.
An M feature whose decomposition is necessary is decomposed.
verification: For an L or XL feature, the check FAILs if the feature is not split. The check consumes the footprint bracket produced by the footprint-scoring convention; it does not verify the scoring itself.

For an M feature, the check FAILs if decomposition is established as necessary (by the planner's own assessment or by reviewer/owner judgment) and the feature is kept whole. If the missing authored criterion leaves necessity undetermined, report UNRESOLVED (needs judgment), not PASS. Do not invent a numeric threshold.

Activation scope: (a footprint task term OR a size-bracket change to M, L or XL) AND the planning phase. Bare 'split'/'decompose' wording with no feature-footprint context does not activate the check.

values: feature size bracket set to M, L or XL

fires: During planning, the planner finalizes a feature whose footprint bracket lands in M, L or XL, whether recognized from the task's own terms (footprint bracket M/L/XL, split feature, decompose feature) or from the feature's size bracket being set to M, L or XL.
doesNotFire: Features whose footprint bracket is XS or S.
Splitting a feature for reasons unrelated to its footprint, such as ownership or release scheduling.
Bare 'split' or 'decompose' wording with no feature-footprint context.

classification.note: Already stack-neutral. The M/L/XL point bands are convention data from the footprint-scoring convention, not stack structure, so they stay in the core rather than the profile.
Planner and plan are process/plan-artifact concepts; no stack term present. Kept verbatim.
The two Bun sentences are merged into one bracket-keyed obligation; neither the L/XL split duty nor the conditional M decompose duty is dropped or strengthened.
'The source gives no criterion' rephrased as 'no authored criterion exists' so the core stands alone; the judgment-but-not-a-free-pass semantics are unchanged.
'Retyping' means redeclaring a component's type to lower its weight; it is a metric-gaming anti-pattern of the footprint metric itself, not a stack construct. Kept.
FAIL disposition for L/XL, stated generically; this text names no detector, validator or finding id. A scope note was added: the check consumes the bracket and does not verify the scoring itself.
FAIL/UNRESOLVED dispositions for M kept, including the instruction not to invent a numeric threshold; 'the missing source criterion' rephrased as 'the missing authored criterion'. No ids named.

Values and llm_judged observability kept. The note ('generic split/decompose alone is not a trigger') has no field in the core fact schema; its semantics are carried by core.activation.doesNotFire and restated in verification.
Alternative change trigger kept; the note's 'either fact is sufficient' OR-semantics are carried by core.activation.fires and restated in verification.
Planning-phase combinator kept as a fact; the note's '(task_term OR change) AND phase' combination is carried by core.activation.fires and restated in verification.

neutralityNotes: bun.json was already stack-neutral: it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so bunOnly is empty and no structural profile data is needed (profileRequirements empty). The footprint bracket scale (XS-S/M/L/XL point bands) is convention data shared with the footprint-scoring convention, not stack structure, so it stays in the core. The activation fact notes ('either fact is sufficient', '(task_term OR change) AND phase=planning', 'generic split/decompose alone is not a trigger') have no field in the closed core fact schema; their semantics are preserved in core.activation.fires, core.activation.doesNotFire and the verification entry on activation scope. Apart from merging the two 'then' sentences into one obligation and dropping the meta reference to 'the source', the agent-facing text is unchanged.
